A type checker tells you what's wrong, so an AI should reach correct code more easily with one. But is that actually true? articles.title: CreateProcess search order turns an executable name into a trust decision
articles.excerpt: CreateProcess search order turns an executable name into a trust decision Windows CreateProcess can launch an executable by name or by full path. When the caller supplies a name without a directory, t…
articles.body: CreateProcess search order turns an executable name into a trust decision Windows CreateProcess can launch an executable by name or by full path. When the caller supplies a name without a directory, the operating system resolves it through a search sequence that includes locations beyond the caller's explicit directory. That behavior is convenient for interactive tools and risky for a privileged service that inherits an attacker-influenced working directory or environment. Microsoft's CreateProcessW documentation lists the search sequence used when the file name does not contain a path. It includes the application's directory, the current directory, system directories, the Windows directory, and directories in PATH in the documented order.

articles.title: I built 59 free browser-based dev tools in vanilla JS — here's what I learned
articles.excerpt: I've been quietly building Antigravity Tools — a collection of 59 free, browser-based developer utilities — and today I'm sharing everything I built and learned. The main constraint I set for myself:…
articles.body: I've been quietly building Antigravity Tools — a collection of 59 free, browser-based developer utilities — and today I'm sharing everything I built and learned. Why vanilla JS? No React, no build step. The main constraint I set for myself: zero dependencies, zero server, zero telemetry . When you paste your JWT token into jwt.io, it goes to their server. When you use an online regex tester, your test strings are logged. I built Antigravity Tools so every operation runs inside your browser, using native APIs. No Node.js backend No npm packages No webpack/vite/parcel No Google Analytics No cookies Everything runs on Web Crypto API , Canvas API , Web Audio API , and IndexedDB — all native to modern browsers.

articles.title: Silent Failures: When an AI Agent Says Done and the Work Is Wrong
articles.excerpt: A customer asks for a refund. The agent checks the order, calls the payments tool, and replies: your refund has been processed, you will see it in three to five days. The conversation closes with a sa…
articles.body: A customer asks for a refund. The agent checks the order, calls the payments tool, and replies: your refund has been processed, you will see it in three to five days. The conversation closes with a satisfied rating. Nothing in the logs is red. Two weeks later the customer writes again, angrier. The money never arrived. The payments call had returned a pending status that the agent read as success, and no one ever looked at what happened next. Nothing crashed, no alert fired, and every dashboard stayed green. The only evidence that anything went wrong was a customer who noticed. This is the silent failure, and it is the subject of this article. We start with the problem and only then look at a way of handling it.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission, the first Mars mission in 20 years. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected.

articles.excerpt: NASA is asking the public to send their names to Titan for an ambitious mission that will see a flying craft explore the Saturn moon in 2034, if all goes according to plan.
articles.body: We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034.
